source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average crossed $4 on July 20, 2026 ($4.003) — first time above $4 in over a month — and reached $4.019 on Monday July 21 (Day 144), up from $3.872 (July 13) as the ceasefire unraveled and Brent surged toward $100. Diesel $5.11. The interim de-escalation collapsed in this window: the US ran 12 consecutive nights of strikes against Iran (through July 22-23), reimposed and actively enforced its naval blockade of Iranian ports, and suffered its first combat deaths since March at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, Jordan (July 17); the Houthis opened a second front with a Red Sea blockade of Saudi Arabia (July 20-22). Brent settled $94.07 on July 22 (+3.4%) and spiked toward $100 intraday July 23 (+6.4%, first time above $100 since late May); WTI settled $86.83 on July 22. Pump prices lag crude by 2-3 weeks, so further increases are likely if the two-chokepoint conflict sustains Brent near $100. Now ~$1.03/gal above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline (~34% higher). The wartime peak was ~$4.56/gal (May 21), below AAA's nominal record of $5.016 (June 14, 2022). Moody's Analytics (NPR, mid-June) estimated at least $132 billion in combined US consumer and taxpayer costs — now a stale undercount that predates the July escalation.
